bottleneck: Telomere extension can rejuvenate cells in culture, but in whole organisms longer telomeres also extend the replicative lifespan of pre-cancerous cells. The trade-off between regeneration and cancer risk is quantitatively unmapped: no one knows a safe telomerase dose, duration, or target tissue. Delivery of telomerase specifically to stem cell compartments without systemic exposure is unsolved, and the long latency of cancer makes any trial's safety readout take decades.
current_state: Telomerase gene therapy extends healthspan in mice. Human applications remain preclinical, blocked by the cancer-risk question no trial can ethically resolve quickly.

sources.title: Gene Therapy: A Breakthrough in Disease Treatment

title: Telomere therapy's cancer trade-off unmapped
why_it_blocks: Aging's molecular clock is readable but not safely adjustable. Until the cancer-regeneration trade-off is quantified, telomere interventions stay in the realm of speculation, and aging research loses one of its most direct levers.
